Mark-sweep, compact, and copy space model

claims.text: HotSpot combines implementation techniques such as generational scavenging and aging, parallel or concurrent work, and compaction; concrete collectors therefore should not be presented as a one-to-one synonym for a single textbook reclamation mechanism.

The reproducible space model demonstrates the intended textbook distinction used by the answer: sweeping may leave separated free holes, while compacting or copying surviving objects can create a contiguous reusable region and copying moves survivors into a target space.

Oracle JDK 25 explains generational collection through the weak generational hypothesis, shows the Serial collector young generation as Eden plus two Survivor spaces, and describes surviving objects being copied between Survivor spaces and aging into old; young collection cost is closely tied to live objects.

Oracle JDK 25 documents Serial, Parallel, G1 and ZGC as the HotSpot collector choices discussed in the tuning guide; Serial uses a single GC thread, Parallel is throughput-oriented and generational, G1 is mostly concurrent and pause-goal-oriented while maintaining high throughput, and ZGC is low-latency-oriented.
Oracle JDK 25 ergonomics selects G1 by default on server-class machines and Serial otherwise, so the answer correctly avoids stating G1 as an unconditional JVM default.

Oracle JDK 25 treats throughput and latency as primary GC measures and describes tradeoffs among pause time, throughput, footprint and promptness, supporting workload-specific selection and measurement instead of absolute collector rules.

Oracle JDK 25 describes G1 as generational, incremental, parallel, mostly concurrent, stop-the-world and evacuating; G1 divides the heap into regions and reclaims space incrementally in stop-the-world pauses while longer global work such as marking can run concurrently.

Oracle JDK 25 G1 guidance recommends starting from defaults and diagnostic GC logging, then addressing specific causes; documented examples include evacuation failure and humongous-object fragmentation, so the answer correctly rejects treating every long pause or Full GC as proof that the collector choice itself is wrong.

findings: The fixed candidate bytes were reviewed source-first against the current canonical/source rows and Oracle JDK 25 primary documentation before historical evidence or remediation records were consulted.

The candidate directly answers the broad GC-algorithm question while separating textbook space-reclamation mechanisms, generational organization and concurrency dimensions from concrete HotSpot collectors.
Version-sensitive claims are bounded to JDK 25 and the server-class default-selection condition; Serial Eden/two-Survivor wording is explicitly scoped rather than universalized.
G1 is correctly treated as a region-based collector combining concurrent work and evacuation, and tuning guidance remains evidence-driven without fabricated production metrics.
